119	  any content comparison. A declared-OPEN position is still typed: `schemaVersion: 2`
120	  passes and moves the id to `437e791c…`.

213	### 2.6 Clone body identity
214	
215	The framed preimage, computed from the prose and hand-checked:
216	
217	```
218	body span "{ return 1; }"            (src/util.ts, bytes 24..37)
219	L0 payload  = 0000000d 7b2072657475726e20313b207d        (raw_byte_len || bytes)
220	final frame component = 00000011 0000000d 7b…7d          (payload_len = raw + 4)
221	bodyIdentity = sha256:09e6886969e59edf13b8058ded5b61074d0bf3343bde1e096e98df56aac9e4eb
222	```
223	
224	`TS-CLONE-N1` computes the *single*-prefix reading and gets
225	`sha256:4950da43…` — a different identity. The contract names which of the two
226	grammatically available readings is admitted, and my independent implementation
227	reproduces the double prefix.
228	
229	`languageVersion` is the **raw 32 bytes** of `SHA-256(C(body-language-version))`,
230	and `body-language-version` is `derived`: I recomputed it from the domain row's
231	`languageVersionBinding` rather than accepting it.
232	
233	**Body language vs provider identity.** The same 13 bytes in `src/util.js`, read
234	by the *same* TypeScript engine universe, mint
235	`sha256:88db5341…` — because `languageId` comes from
236	`bodyLanguageByVariant[<suffix variant>]` (`js` → `javascript`), never from the
237	domain row's own `language` field (which names the engine). `TS-CLONE-N2` refuses
238	a `rust`-framed body under a TypeScript universe.
239	
240	**Grammar parse vs compiler parse.** The identical Rust body span read by the
241	grammar bundle mints `sha256:216ecad0…` against the compiler's
242	`sha256:74746ea0…` — different `compilerName`
243	(`opensip-grammar-bundle` vs `rustc`) and a different dialect branch
244	(`{grammarVariant:"rs"}` vs `{edition:2021}`).
245	
246	**L0 vs a normalized level.** `RS-CLONE-L1` builds the framed token stream
247	(`u32be count || (u16be kind_len||kind || u32be val_len||val)*`) at `L1-lexical`
248	with a retained, re-hashable level specification. At L0 I recomputed the payload
249	from the fact's own anchor (a real source join); at L1 what is required is
250	retained-preimage custody plus the framed-identity check — which qualifies no
251	normalizer, exactly as the contract says.

459	### 2.13 Sufficiency and repair
460	
461	`Atom.minResolution` and `EvidenceRequirement.minResolution` are **rung names**;
462	the flat enum is exactly the union of the thirteen ladders (verified equal) and is
463	**necessary only** — membership of *this atom's relation's* ladder is sufficient
464	and is enforced at admission. Satisfaction is ladder-index comparison inside one
465	relation; a cross-relation comparison is a **refusal**, never a truth value
466	(`SUF-N1…N6`).
467	
468	Qualifying and insufficient pairs at all three levels: `declares@syntactic`
469	(qualifying) vs `imports` at the weaker `syntactic-specifier` rung;
470	`references@resolved-binding` under `universal-negative/forbid/forbid` with
471	`state: complete` and `exportsClosed: closed` — the **only** shape under which an
472	authoritative no-consumer claim is eligible — vs the same atom with one
473	`computed-member-access` edge (`resolution-incomplete`, cause carried by
474	`resolutionCompleteness`, `nativeCause` null **by design**) and vs a
475	budget-exhausted `partial` stage; `types@checked` with `annotated` derivation
476	(qualifying) vs `compiler-inferred` under `declared-only`
477	(`derivation-policy-unmet`, carried by `derivationKinds` and scoped to relation
478	`types`) vs a fact at the weaker `annotated` rung.
479	
480	`SUF-2` reproduces the removed early exit: confidence 100000 against a floor of
481	900000 yields `confidence-floor-unmet` for a one-rung `clones` requirement under
482	`partial-ok`, and 1000000 satisfies.
483	
484	The repair evidence requirements, the five-field `closedWorld` projection (with
485	`dynamicDispatch` and `reasons` **dropped**), the authority boundary (the
486	projection grants nothing; authority stays the sealed Run named by
487	`evidenceRunId`, including the two members the descriptor does not carry), the
488	target-relative reading of `dynamicDispatch`, and the imported-observation
489	boundary (`observable-unhit` ≠ unused; one window is never universal non-use;
490	runtime coverage is never OpenSIP Coverage; mandatory source correspondence) all
491	reconstruct — except for the one field named in MUST-1.
492	
493	---
494	
495	## 3. Independent vector inventory
496	
497	78 vector groups. **83 discriminating negative controls**, every one refusing with
498	a typed cause, **zero** unexpectedly admitted:
499	
500	| Group | Negatives | Covers |
501	|---|---|---|
502	| `CAP-N*` | 12 | all four ADM gates + CVE1 |
503	| `TS-NEGATIVES` | 26 | context/universe joins, hidden inputs, frames, anchor law, RC-0/1/2, totality, cross-universe discharge |
504	| `RS-OWNERSHIP-NEGATIVES` | 6 | every branch of the Rust dialect selection law |
505	| `RS-NEGATIVES` | 18 | clone disclosure derivation + Rust hidden/mismatched inputs |
506	| `SY-NEGATIVES` | 12 | grammar class law, capability boundaries, suffix law |
507	| `SUF-NEGATIVES` | 6 | atom vocabulary and cross-relation comparison |
508	| `TS-CLONE-N1/N2`, `TS-CFG-1b` | 3 | body framing and record-shape controls |
509	
510	Highlights I want to name explicitly because they are the ones a permissive
511	implementation would pass:
512	
513	* `TS-N13` — a `file@enumerated` fact of **another universe** does **not**
514	  discharge this scope's totality obligation. The view-level fact/scope join is
515	  existential, so without the five-coordinate `matchOn` a TypeScript fact would
516	  pay a syntax-universe scope's debt. Refuses.
517	* `TS-N23` — a raw canonical payload offered where an `h-identity` **frame** is
518	  required fails on the prefix; `TS-N24` — a single flipped bit in a retained
519	  frame fails; `TS-N25` — an unregistered H domain refuses; `TS-N26` — the
520	  retained context set must equal `plan.nativeContextDigests` **exactly**, in both
521	  directions.
522	* `RS-N19`/`RS-N20` — `configProjectionSha256` carrying the raw **file** digest,
523	  or raw SHA-256 of `C(record)`, both refuse. All three values are distinct in my
524	  vector (`RS-DIG-1`), as the contract requires.
525	* `RS-N17` — a retained `PreparedOutputSetV3` that **no universe selected** is
526	  refused: bytes in custody never enter a resolution by being in custody.
527	* `RS-N7…N11` — an empty clone view under partial ownership cannot claim
528	  `complete`; `unknown` with a null deficiency is an undisclosed gap; an unrelated
529	  but schema-valid `budget-exhausted`, a null cause and a wrong ownership cause
530	  each refuse separately, so the four faults stay separable.
531	
532	---
533	
534	## 4. Issues
535	
536	### MUST-1 — `EvidenceRequirement.deficiency` cannot express four of the nine outcomes its only producer emits
537	
538	**Selector:**
539	`docs/coop/design-corrections/workflows/schemas/repair.schema.json#/$defs/EvidenceRequirement/properties/deficiency`
540	→ `urn:opensip:product-v1:workflows:common#/$defs/D9Deficiency`.
541	
542	The field's only defined producer is native §4.6 `sufficiency_v2`, whose outcome
543	vocabulary is `DeficiencyV2`
544	(`native/native-evidence.schemas.v2.json#/$defs/DeficiencyV2`, and the §10
545	precedence list). Four of its nine members are **not** in `D9Deficiency`:
546	
547	```
548	derivation-policy-unmet   external-consumers-unknown
549	input-closure-incomplete  resolution-incomplete
550	```
551	
552	`resolution-incomplete` is exactly what §4.6 step 6 mandates for a
553	`universal-negative` under `unresolvedEdgePolicy: forbid` over an affected target
554	— the case a destructive unused-code recipe turns on, and the case workflows §6
555	routes through this record. Three conforming readings exist and they disagree:
556	write the D9-mapped `verdict-indeterminate` (collapsing all four successor
557	members and destroying the per-requirement distinction native §10 went to length
558	to preserve); write the `sufficiency_v2` value (schema-invalid for four of nine);
559	or omit the optional field (dropping the disclosure). No document states which
560	vocabulary the field carries, and no mapping is published in either direction.
561	
562	The `DomainDetailCode` route native §10 names does **not** resolve it: that
563	vocabulary covers a *different* five members
564	(`budget-exhausted`, `derivation-policy-unmet`, `external-consumers-unknown`,
565	`input-closure-incomplete`, `resolution-incomplete` — but not
566	`confidence-floor-unmet`, `language-tier-unsupported`, `provider-unavailable`,
567	`required-relation-missing`). The union of the two vocabularies covers all nine;
568	**neither single field does**, and `EvidenceRequirement.deficiency` is a single
569	field. Vector `GAP-1`.
570	
571	**Remedy (one of):** re-type the field to `DeficiencyV2`; or state normatively
572	that it carries the D9-mapped value and publish `DeficiencyV2 → D9Deficiency`; or
573	split it into a D9 field plus a native-cause field. Any of the three closes it;
574	what an implementer must not have to do is choose.
575	
576	### MUST-2 — `TypeScriptConfigGraphV1.nodes[].kind` has no published derivation, and it is hashed into `RunId`
577	
578	**Selector:**
579	`docs/coop/design-corrections/native/native-evidence.schemas.v2.json#/$defs/TypeScriptConfigGraphV1/properties/nodes/items/properties/kind`;
580	prose at `native-evidence.md` §2.2 line 940.
581	
582	The prose says *"Node kind agrees with its path as specified by the schema and
583	native admission."* The schema supplies only the three-member enum
584	`{tsconfig, jsconfig, other}`. No path→kind rule appears anywhere in this kit,
585	and no `native admission` rule for it is published.
586	
587	`kind` sits inside the hashed record: `tsconfigGraphHash` is the raw SHA-256 of
588	`C(TypeScriptConfigGraphV1)`; `TypeScriptUniverseV2ResolvedInputs` **requires**
589	it and `bind_typescript_universe` checks equality; the universe H identity is
590	`fact.sourceUniverse` and `subject-scope.sourceUniverse`, hence `fact2`,
591	`scope2`, `coverage2`, `view2`, `evidence2`, `seal2` and `run2`.
592	
593	Two natural readings disagree on real files:
594	
595	* **basename exactly** — `tsconfig.json` → `tsconfig`, `jsconfig.json` →
596	  `jsconfig`, everything else → `other` (what I used); or
597	* **basename prefix** — any `tsconfig*.json` → `tsconfig` (the widespread
598	  `tsconfig.build.json` / `tsconfig.base.json` convention).
599	
600	Discriminating file: `tsconfig.build.json` reached as a base of the entry —
601	`other` under the first reading, `tsconfig` under the second, two different
602	`tsconfigGraphHash` values and **two different RunIds for one repository**.
603	The `configOrigin` derivation does not pin it: `other` and `tsconfig` both derive
604	`tsconfig`, and a **non-entry** node's kind affects no derived value at all yet is
605	still committed to the identity. Vector `GAP-2`.
606	
607	This is the contract's own standard. CB4-SHOULD-2 elevated exactly this class of
608	defect for `analysis-spec.requestedCapabilities[].capabilityId` — *"two conforming
609	hosts requesting the same analysis of the same unit therefore mint different
610	`analysisSpecDigest`s, different `PlanId`s and different `RunId`s, which defeats
611	independent replay across machines"* — and closed it by naming the vocabulary
612	authority. The same closure is owed here.
613	
614	**Remedy:** publish the path→kind rule beside the enum (a `x-opensip-vocabulary`
615	annotation naming the authority would match the pattern already used for
616	`capabilityId`), and state it for non-entry nodes as well as the entry.
617	
618	### SHOULD-1 — no published map from the closed command name vocabulary to `MutationOperation`
619	
620	**Selectors:** `workflows/command-inventory.v1.json#/commands[]` (45 commands, the
621	declared **sole** command list, whose `Command` record carries **no**
622	`mutationClass` field) and
623	`workflows/schemas/repair.schema.json#/$defs/MutationOperation` (24 members).
624	
625	Three of the ten mutation-class commands have no same-named operation:
626	`waive`, `policy-init`, `baseline-upgrade`. Their operations
627	(`waiver-change`, `policy-write`, `baseline-upgrade-apply`) are inferable but
628	unpublished. `mutationClass` is a **public** envelope field, and workflows §1
629	makes `MutationReplayScopeV1.operation` equal to it, so it enters the
630	`H("workflow.mutation-intent", scope)` preimage of the published
631	`idempotencyKey`. Vector `WF-11` / `GAP-3`.
632	
633	Bounded impact, which is why this is SHOULD and not MUST: `requestId` is
634	host-minted and unique per invocation, so a spelling difference cannot cause a
635	false or missed dedupe *across* hosts, and the key grants no authority. What is
636	lost is a consumer's ability to derive the expected `mutationClass` from the
637	contracts alone.
638	
639	### SHOULD-2 — the Coverage-partition "without omissions" clause has no decidable referent for symbol relations
640	
641	**Selectors:** `identity-and-evidence.md` §3, *"Coverage scopes partition the
642	claimed universe without overlaps or omissions"*, against `native-evidence.md`
643	§1.2, *"Which relations owe totality is stated in the relation registry
644	(`coverageTotality`), where only `file` has a row, and never inferred."*
645	
646	The overlap half is decidable (pairwise disjointness of subjects within one
647	`(snapshotId, relation, resolution, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse)` key). The
648	omission half is not, for the nine `symbol`-kind relations: native §1.2 itself
649	states that the enumerator's attribution of symbols to files is **trusted and not
650	re-derivable from the retained Run**, and no document publishes an enumeration of
651	the symbol universe. Two conforming readings — "the claimed universe" as the union
652	of the scopes' own committed subjects (making the clause vacuous and the sentence
653	an overlap rule) or as what exists (making it unenforceable and inconsistent with
654	the `coverageTotality` registry). Vector `GAP-4`.
655	
656	I used the registry reading and enforced overlap-freedom separately. The registry
657	statement is the more specific successor and does resolve it in practice; what is
658	missing is the reconciliation in the text, which an implementer must currently
659	supply.
660	
661	### Advisory (non-blocking)
662	
663	* **ADV-1 — `js-synthesized` recognition vs §1.4 U-1.** §1.2's recognition row
664	  admits a `tsjs` unit for *"`package.json` present **or any** `.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx`
665	  file under the unit"*, while U-1 requires a directory to hold one of the three
666	  markers to yield a unit at all. Under U-1 the second disjunct is unreachable and
667	  a directory of bare `.js` files is **not** a unit (its files are `grammar-only`).
668	  U-1 governs — it is the specific model with the closed `WorkspaceUnitV2` record
669	  and the exactly-once `FileMembershipRowV1` law — but an implementer reading §1.2
670	  alone would mint units for bare-`.js` directories, changing both membership and
671	  the Plan. Vector `GAP-5`; I used U-1.
672	* **ADV-2 — the scope of `native.confidence.v1`.** §4.8 defines the method as
673	  *"declared-exact: every admitted checked fact is 1000000 under its universe; **no
674	  value below 1000000 is produced by a native provider**"*. The second clause is
675	  unscoped, yet §4.6's own named regression case exercises a `clones` fact at
676	  `confidenceMillionths` 100000, and sufficiency step 3 compares the field for
677	  every relation. The clause must be read as scoped to the `types@checked` method
678	  it defines, or step 3 and that regression case are both unreachable. Vector
679	  `GAP-6`; I used the types-scoped reading.
680	* **ADV-3 — the successor D9 artifact is owed, and the contract says so.** Native
681	  §10 states plainly that `d9-exit-contract.v1.14.json` keeps its bytes and that
682	  publishing the successor D9 artifact belongs to that unit. A checker reading the
683	  inherited artifact alone would refuse a lawful `host-invariant` termination. I
684	  record this because it is a live cross-unit dependency for implementation, not
685	  because the design is unclear — it is disclosed, bounded, and correctly attributed.
686	
687	---
688	
689	## 5. What I had to invent, and what I deliberately did not
690	
691	**Invented — and I flag each as an assumption, not a reconstruction:**
692	
693	1. The path→`kind` rule for `TypeScriptConfigGraphV1` nodes (MUST-2). I chose
694	   exact-basename matching. It changes `RunId`.
695	2. The value written to `EvidenceRequirement.deficiency` for the four
696	   inexpressible outcomes (MUST-1). I left the field absent in my vectors rather
697	   than write a value the schema refuses or a value that loses the distinction.
698	3. The `waive` → `waiver-change` mapping (SHOULD-1).
699	4. The referent of "the claimed universe" (SHOULD-2). I used the registry reading.
700	
701	**Algorithm freedom deliberately left to implementation — not gaps.** I did not
702	count any of these as findings: the clone `near-v1` shingling, the `tsjs-erasure-v1`
703	projection details, query planning (explicitly an optimization only, held to
704	agree with a retained full scan), the choice of which spans a producer cites for a
705	code fact (a real statement about what it read, with no cross-provider anchor
706	identity promised), the internal diagnostic key space, and the physical storage
707	carrier. Each of these is a genuine implementation choice whose *public* boundary
708	is contracted.
709	
710	**I did not have to invent** — and want to record it, because these are the places
711	a weaker contract would have forced me to: the `subjectScopeCommitment` producing
712	recipe (§4.1a, closed, and it is the *same* digest as `scope2`); the
713	`unitId` preimage (published four-field record, `derived` retention, not an opaque
714	digest); the L0 double-length-prefix reading (named explicitly); the `libSelection`
715	→ component `fold` (named as full non-tailored default lowercase, with the three
716	discriminating code points and a declared UCD version); which of `projectionSha256`
717	/ `configProjectionSha256` / `raw(C(record))` each field carries; the dialect
718	selection order and its per-step causes; the syntax capability law's inventory
719	exemption at **both** boundaries; and the `(deficiency, nativeCause)` carrier per
720	row. Every one of those would have been an invention in a less complete kit.
721	
722	---
723	
724	## 6. Limitations of this review
725	
726	* This is a **design reference exercise**. Nothing here qualifies a product,
727	  authorizes implementation, or awards a readiness grade. Passing my checks is not
728	  product qualification.
729	* Every OS, filesystem, compiler, Cargo, provider, cryptographic and SQLite
730	  observation in my vectors is a **synthetic trusted observation** — an assumption,
731	  never native enforcement proof. I executed no compiler, no repository code, no
732	  provider and no ledger. Real fsync/SQLite/process-death, ACL and O_NOFOLLOW
733	  custody races, concurrent readers and writers, cross-machine replay, hostile
734	  archive import and renderer parity remain future qualification work, and I
735	  treated their absence as such rather than as a design defect.
736	* My closures, trees, manifests and signatures are synthetic; a signature check
737	  proves only that a signer signed those bytes, and I made no trust claim.
738	* I did not review the security unit's S4/S5/S6/S7/S9 time, root-chain, revocation
739	  and lease machinery beyond the joins the reconstruction needed (S3 discovery,
740	  S10/S10.1/S10.2 authorization, S12/S12.1 refusal projection). A separate pass
741	  would be needed to reconstruct those.
742	* Byte-level values in my vectors depend on my synthetic inputs. What is
743	  independently meaningful is the **recipe** each value was computed by, the
744	  refusals, and the disagreements between two conforming readings — not the digests
745	  themselves.
746	* I verified only the schemas the kit contains. Where a document is named but
747	  absent from the kit by design (author reference models, fixtures, checkers), I
748	  reconstructed the law from the prose rather than assuming the repository omitted
749	  it, and none of those absences blocked a promised vector.
750	
751	---
752	
753	## 7. Verdict
754	
755	**CHANGES_REQUIRED.**
756	
757	This is a strong contract set. Every promised vector was constructible from these
758	inputs alone, with one exception (MUST-1, where the schema refuses the value its
759	own producer emits), and the two identity-critical recipes I most expected to be
760	under-specified — the `subjectScopeCommitment` producing recipe and the Rust
761	compilation-unit dialect selection — are closed, precise, and reproduced exactly
762	by an independent implementation. The design's strongest property is the closing
763	digest law: **no default**, so a 64-hex field without an annotation refuses. That
764	law is what let me find MUST-2 mechanically, by asking of every field I had to
765	populate "what must this value *be*?" — and finding one hashed field where the
766	contract answers only "as specified by the schema and native admission", and
767	neither does.
768	
769	The two MUST issues are narrow, precisely located and independently fixable, and
770	neither is architectural: one is a field type that must name its vocabulary, the
771	other is a derivation rule that must be written down beside a field that is
772	already correctly hashed. Both are the same class of defect the contract set has
773	already corrected twice by its own initiative (CB3-MUST-1's ladder, CB4-SHOULD-2's
774	capability vocabulary), and both would defeat exactly the property the set most
775	insists on: independent replay across machines. That is why they block rather than
776	advise. The two SHOULD issues are reconciliations the text owes a reader, not
777	choices the design has failed to make.
778	
779	I would expect a corrected revision to be reconstructable without invention.

1716	### 4.5 Closed-world assumptions (feedback 7)
1717	
1718	`ClosedWorldV2` = `{exportsClosed: closed|open|unknown, entryPointsRecognized:
1719	all|partial|none, nonliteralLoading: none|present, externalConsumers:
1720	none-declared|possible|unknown, dynamicDispatch: resolved|present|not-applicable,
1721	reasons[], deadCodeRepairEligible}`. `exportsClosed=closed` requires **every**
1722	ingredient:
1723	
1724	1. the manifest publishes nothing (`package.json` without `exports`, `main`,
1725	   `module`, `types`, `bin`, `browser`, `files` or `workspaces`, with
1726	   `private:true`; or a Cargo package with `[[bin]]` targets only);
1727	2. `entryPointsRecognized=all` (explicit origins or a recognizer with no
1728	   `unresolvedChoices`);
1729	3. `nonliteralLoading=none` (no `require-nonliteral`, `dynamic-import-nonliteral`,
1730	   `reflective-access`, `indirect-eval` edges in the universe);
1731	4. `externalConsumers=none-declared` (the user/policy declares no non-repository
1732	   consumers: no published subpath, no sibling deployment reading the tree).
1733	
1734	`private:true` alone is `unknown` (`private-true-alone-is-not-closed`). A
1735	universal-negative predicate on an exported subject of an `open`/`unknown`
1736	universe with `externalConsumerPolicy=forbid` reports `external-consumers-unknown`.
1737	
1738	**Dynamic edges propagate.** `affected_targets` marks every subject a dynamic
1739	edge could reach: `targetScope=module` marks all exports of `targetModule`;
1740	`universe` marks all subjects of the universe; `external`/`unknown` marks every
1741	exported subject. A universal negative about an affected subject is
1742	`resolution-incomplete` even when the entry's own count is zero for that relation
1743	(`dynamic-edge-propagates-to-universe-and-external`).
1744	
1745	**No missing entry point permits dead-code repair.** `deadCodeRepairEligible` is
1746	true only with `exportsClosed=closed`, `entryPointsRecognized=all` and no
1747	nonliteral loading; the workflow owner's repair prerequisites consume this flag
1748	(H-5). Unrecognized frameworks yield `entryPointsRecognized=none`
1749	(`framework-unrecognized-entry-points-none`); a config that would need evaluation
1750	yields `partial`.
1751	
1752	### 4.6 Sufficiency v2 (replaces `$.sufficiency`)
1753	
1754	Evaluated in this order; every applicable cause is collected and the most specific
1755	by §10 precedence is reported. `satisfied=true` may carry `disclosures`.
1756	
1757	1. Relation absent from the view → `required-relation-missing`.
1758	2. Rung below `minResolution` → the rung-unavailable cause (`language-tier-unsupported`, `provider-unavailable`, `input-closure-incomplete`, `budget-exhausted`) else `required-relation-missing`.
1759	3. `confidenceMillionths < minConfidenceMillionths` → `confidence-floor-unmet`.
1760	4. Relation `types` with `derivationPolicy=declared-only` and any `compiler-inferred` derivation in the view → `derivation-policy-unmet`.
1761	5. `completeness=complete` and `coverage≠complete` → the entry's own deficiency.
1762	6. `quantifier=universal-negative`: state `partial` or `not-attempted` → `resolution-incomplete` regardless of policy; state `incomplete` or target affected by a dynamic edge → `forbid`: `resolution-incomplete`; `disclose`: disclosure `{unresolved-edges, count, classes}`.
1763	7. `quantifier=universal-negative`, target exported and `exportsClosed≠closed` → `forbid`: `external-consumers-unknown`; `assume-closed`: disclosure.
1764	8. Dependencies (`dependsOn`) recursively (depth ≤ 4) with `partial-ok` for existential requirements and the parent's quantifier/policies for universal negatives.
1765	
1766	There is no early exit. A one-rung relation under `existential` with
1767	`partial-ok` passes step 5 vacuously but still runs steps 1–4 and 8: the former
1768	step 9 shortcut ("satisfied outright") returned before the confidence floor and
1769	let confidence 100000 pass a floor of 900000; it was removed (post-reset
1770	SHOULD-4) and the regression case
1771	`sufficiency-v2-confidence-floor-precedes-one-rung-existential-shortcut`
1772	checks that v2 and the retained v1 oracle both yield `confidence-floor-unmet`
1773	for `clones` at 100000 under floor 900000, and `satisfied` at 1000000.
1774	
1775	### 4.7 Positive coverage case (`positive-static-consumer`)
1776	
1777	Module A exports `foo` and `bar`; module B does `import {foo} from './a'; foo();`
1778	No computed access, no dynamic import, `package.json private:true` without
1779	published entries, explicit entry points, no external consumers declared.
1780	Provider emits `references@resolved-binding` for `foo`, zero `unresolved-edge`
1781	facts, the stage completes, `resolutionCompleteness.complete`,
1782	`exportsClosed=closed`. Then "no consumer of `foo`" → satisfied=false by evidence;
1783	"no consumer of `bar`" under `universal-negative/forbid/forbid` → satisfied=true
1784	with no deficiency. That is the only shape under which an authoritative
1785	no-consumer claim is eligible. No provider verdict exists.
1786	
1787	### 4.8 Type derivation provenance (feedback 12)
1788	
1789	The v1 draft capped JSDoc-free JavaScript type facts at `confidenceMillionths ≤
1790	900000`. That number had no evidence rationale: a compiler-inferred type is exact
1791	under the admitted universe, and JSDoc presence is not a calibrated probability.
1792	Replacement: every `types@checked` fact carries `TypeDerivationV1` =
1793	`{derivationKind: annotated|jsdoc-declared|compiler-inferred, confidenceMillionths:
1794	1000000, confidenceMethod: "native.confidence.v1", checkJs, limitations}`.
1795	`native.confidence.v1` is the versioned, conformance-bound method
1796	"declared-exact: every admitted checked fact is 1000000 under its universe; no
1797	value below 1000000 is produced by a native provider". Rule authors express
1798	"declared types only" through `derivationPolicy=declared-only` (§4.2), which
1799	yields the typed `derivation-policy-unmet` deficiency, not a fake percentage.
1800	`checkJs` is recorded because it changes diagnostics, not derivation.
1801	
1802	---
1803	
1804	## 5. Native execution boundary (AR-07)
1805	
1806	### 5.1 Principal class `repository-code` and its joins (R4)
1807	
1808	The security contract S10 registers principal class `repository-code`
1809	(`RepoExecutionGrantV2`, execution classes `build-script | proc-macro |
1810	test-runner`). One principal, three current spellings, joined explicitly and
1811	checked by schema constants:
1812	
1813	| Where | Spelling | Role |
1814	|---|---|---|
1815	| security S10 / `AuthorizedExecutionV2.principalClass` | `repository-code` | principal class of the admitted grant |

2275	## 10. Deficiencies, precedence and D9 mapping
2276	
2277	`DeficiencyV2` = fact-plane v1 values + `input-closure-incomplete`,
2278	`derivation-policy-unmet`, `resolution-incomplete`, `external-consumers-unknown`.
2279	Precedence (most specific first): `language-tier-unsupported`,
2280	`provider-unavailable`, `input-closure-incomplete`, `budget-exhausted`,
2281	`confidence-floor-unmet`, `derivation-policy-unmet`, `resolution-incomplete`,
2282	`external-consumers-unknown`, `required-relation-missing`.
2283	
2284	**Existing D9 codes only (R7).** No successor, interim or competing code exists in
2285	this contract; `d9_successor_codes()` is the empty list and `d9_map` refuses a row
2286	that names one. The native `deficiency` and `nativeCause` travel as **typed
2287	detail** inside the `coverage2` record (`CoverageResultV3.entry.deficiency` /
2288	`nativeCause`) that the host termination names by its `coverageId`; no D9 enum
2289	changes anywhere.
2290	
2291	**The Cause column is not one field.** This column previously read `Cause
2292	(nativeCause)` throughout, and three of its rows then named values the closed
2293	`NativeCause` enum cannot express: `computed-member-access`, `exports-open` and
2294	`compiler-inferred` each fail schema validation as a `nativeCause`. The only
2295	representable value for those rows was `null` — which that enum's own
2296	description defines as *a disclosure was owed and not made*, the exact argument
2297	that added the three `body-language-*` members. Worse, nothing compared the pair
2298	to anything, so a `resolution-incomplete` entry carrying the unrelated but
2299	schema-valid `lockfile-missing`, or relabelled `capability-missing`, or a
2300	`derivation-policy-unmet` over an empty `derivationKinds`, each closed a Run.
2301	
2302	The correction names the carrier per row rather than adding enum members, and
2303	that is a decision on the merits, not on compatibility: `resolution-incomplete`
2304	has a genuinely **set-valued** cause — an entry can exhibit up to all sixteen
2305	`UnresolvedEdgeKindV1` classes at once — so a scalar could only lose information
2306	or force an arbitrary pick, which is the multi-cause defect itself. All three
2307	rows already have closed, structured, independently derived carriers **in the
2308	same entry**: `resolutionCompleteness` (whose `unresolvedEdgeClasses` RC-2
2309	already forces to equal the admitted `unresolved-edge` facts of the view),
2310	`closedWorld.exportsClosed`, and `derivationKinds`. **No enum changes anywhere** —
2311	not `NativeCause`, not `DeficiencyV2`, not `UnresolvedEdgeKindV1`, not the public
2312	`DomainDetailCode` registry, and no D9 class, code or exit.
2313	
2314	Where the Carrier column says a field other than `nativeCause`, `nativeCause` is
2315	`null` **by design** and that null is no longer an escape: admission refuses
2316	unless the named field actually carries the cause. The pairing is closed in
2317	`native-evidence.schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry`, derived
2318	at the producer boundary in `admit_coverage_result_v3` and therefore re-derived
2319	at retained Run closure, which re-runs that exact admission over the retained
2320	payload (`native.coverage-cause-*`, `PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION`).
2321	
2322	| Native detail | Cause carrier and lawful value | `nativeCause` | D9 class (host-owned) | Existing code | Typed detail carrier |
2323	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
2324	| `input-closure-incomplete` | `entry.nativeCause` — one of `missing-dependency-source`, `lockfile-missing`, `source-replacement-outside-snapshot`, `generated-output-unavailable`, `generated-file-missing`, `generated-file-out-of-bounds`, `no-program-unit`, `node-modules-outside-read-set`, `config-flag-stripped`, `body-language-ownership-missing`, `body-language-owner-unenumerated`, `body-language-owner-ambiguous` | **required** | `indeterminate` (3) | `VERDICT.INDETERMINATE` | coverage2 record |
2325	| `resolution-incomplete` | `entry.resolutionCompleteness` — `state` ∈ {`incomplete`, `partial`, `not-attempted`} names the stage condition, and `unresolvedEdgeClasses` carries **every** applicable class at once | `null` | `indeterminate` (3) | `VERDICT.INDETERMINATE` | coverage2 record |
2326	| `external-consumers-unknown` | `entry.closedWorld.exportsClosed` ∈ {`open`, `unknown`} — the values the old cell spelled `exports-open`, `exports-unknown` | `null` | `indeterminate` (3) | `VERDICT.INDETERMINATE` | coverage2 record |
2327	| `derivation-policy-unmet` | relation **must be `types`** (§4.7 / `sufficiency_v2` give no other relation a derivation policy) **and** `entry.derivationKinds` must contain `compiler-inferred` | `null` | `indeterminate` (3) | `VERDICT.INDETERMINATE` | coverage2 record |
2328	| `provider-unavailable` | `entry.nativeCause` — `capability-missing` or `linker-unavailable` where one applies; the row is otherwise self-describing (incl. missing identity tokens) | optional | `indeterminate` (3) | `COVERAGE.PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` | coverage2 record |
2329	| `language-tier-unsupported` | `entry.nativeCause` = `capability-missing` — the admitted universe's selected grammars do not bear the requested `relation@rung` (§1.2 syntax-only capability law); **no other cause is lawful here** | **required** | `indeterminate` (3) | `VERDICT.INDETERMINATE` | coverage2 record |
2330	| `budget-exhausted` | `entry.resolutionCompleteness.stageTerminal` = `budget-exhausted` — the stage terminal the old cell referred to parenthetically | `null` | `indeterminate` (3) | `COVERAGE.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` | coverage2 record |
2331	| `confidence-floor-unmet` | **none in the entry** — the floor is `RequirementV2.minConfidenceMillionths` and the entry carries only its own `confidenceMillionths`, so the comparison is the sufficiency evaluation's. Stated as a limit rather than given an invented entry-level predicate | `null` | `indeterminate` (3) | `VERDICT.INDETERMINATE` | coverage2 record |
2332	| `required-relation-missing` | **none in the entry** — a sufficiency verdict about a relation the view carries *no* entry for, so an entry can never be its own evidence | `null` | `indeterminate` (3) | `VERDICT.INDETERMINATE` | coverage2 record |
2333	
2334	A `null` deficiency requires a `null` cause: a cause without a deficiency names
2335	why nothing went wrong.
2336	
2337	**Some rows are scoped by relation, because their owning law is.** `§4.7` and
2338	`sufficiency_v2` apply `derivationPolicy` only where the relation is `types` and
2339	the requirement asks `declared-only`; no other relation has a derivation policy,
2340	so no other relation's entry can be short of one. Checking the `derivationKinds`
2341	carrier *alone* let a `references` entry that merely carried the same array value
2342	declare this deficiency, and a complete Run admitted it. The registry row now
2343	carries the owning `relations` list and admission refuses an entry outside it.
2344	
2345	This is **declaration support, not an obligation**, and the two must not be
2346	confused. Enforced: an entry that *declares* `derivation-policy-unmet` is for
2347	`types` and actually carries `compiler-inferred`. Not enforced, and deliberately
2348	so: whether a given requirement *demands* it. `compiler-inferred` types are exact
2349	under the admitted universe, carry no probabilistic confidence, and are entirely
2350	valid under `derivationPolicy=any`; they become a deficiency only under
2351	`declared-only`, which is `sufficiency_v2`'s question against a `RequirementV2`
2352	and is never derived from a Coverage entry. Both directions are held by controls.
2353	
2354	**Multiple simultaneous causes, and precedence.** An entry carries **one**
2355	deficiency and **every** carrier at the same time — but *what each carrier
2356	retains differs*, and an earlier revision of this paragraph generalised the
2357	strongest case to all of them by saying the scalar "loses nothing". Accurately,
2358	per carrier:
2359	
2360	- `resolutionCompleteness.unresolvedEdgeClasses` is a genuine **set** and retains
2361	  *every* applicable unresolved class at once, already forced by RC-2 to equal
2362	  the admitted `unresolved-edge` facts of the view. Here nothing is lost, and
2363	  this is why enum members would have been the wrong fix.
2364	- `closedWorld` and `derivationKinds` are independent fields that retain their
2365	  own state whatever the declared deficiency is.
2366	- `input-closure-incomplete`'s carrier is a **single scalar** `NativeCause`, and
2367	  a Run can genuinely be missing several inputs at once — two absent crates, or
2368	  an absent crate *and* an unavailable generated file. For that row the retained
2369	  cause is a **selected** one, not the full set.
2370	
2371	**The selected-scalar limitation, stated rather than engineered around.** The
2372	producer names the cause it acted on; Run closure checks that the named cause is
2373	lawful for the deficiency and cannot enumerate the inputs that were not named.
2374	What *is* fully retained beside it is the rest of the entry and the Run's own
2375	evidence — the missing dependency sources, prepared rows and generated files are
2376	retained records in their own right — so a consumer needing the complete set
2377	reads those, not the scalar. **No multi-cause format is introduced** merely to
2378	make this paragraph true: the bounded source and ownership laws are unchanged and
2379	the limitation is published so no consumer reads the scalar as exhaustive.
2380	
2381	Which single member is declared when several
2382	apply is the precedence order above, applied by the owning sufficiency
2383	evaluation against a **Requirement**. That selection is deliberately **not**
2384	re-derived from the entry alone, and the limit is stated rather than worked
2385	around: several conditions are requirement-relative (external-consumer state
2386	matters only for a universal negative about an exported target; the confidence
2387	floor lives in the Requirement), and **RC-3** makes `coverage: complete` with
2388	`state: incomplete` and *no* deficiency a valid honest entry. Forcing a
2389	deficiency out of exhibited entry evidence would refuse lawful Runs. What is
2390	decidable from the entry, and what is therefore enforced, is the other
2391	direction: a **declared** deficiency must be **supported** by the entry's own
2392	committed evidence.
2393	
2394	**Retained and public routes are different, and both are named.** *Retained*:
2395	the whole `ViewEntryV3` lives inside the `coverage2` record whose payload and
2396	schema digests the Run commits, so every carrier above is retained evidence a
2397	verifier re-derives. *Public*: the **deficiency** projects outward as its own
2398	closed `DomainDetailCode` — `resolution-incomplete`, `external-consumers-unknown`
2399	and `derivation-policy-unmet` are already members — and the **cause** travels as
2400	typed detail in the `coverage2` record the host termination names by its
2401	`coverageId`, exactly as this section has always said for the
2402	`nativeCause`-carried rows. No new public code is added for this projection of a lawful entry's deficiency and cause. The refusal branches later in this section separately add four public detail codes; those additions do not change this projection.
2403	
2404	### Admission and event routes (existing; unchanged rows)
2405	
2406	These are the pre-existing five-column routes. They were left running on after the
2407	new deficiency table above with no header of their own; the header is restored and
2408	the rows are untouched. The two closing rows carry the admission conditions the
2409	capability-vocabulary guard introduced.

389	## 6. Repair preview, apply, verify (AR-08)
390	
391	Three separately authorized steps; schemas in `repair.schema.json`.
392	
393	**Preview** (`repair-preview`, Query class) requires an **authoritative** evidence Run
394	(`REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_NOT_AUTHORITATIVE` for ephemeral) whose availability is retained
395	and whose sealed assurance is replayable (else the plan is not applicable with
396	`REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_UNAVAILABLE`), a recipe closure admitted under current trust
397	(`REPAIR.RECIPE_TRUST_REVOKED`; an absent admission is also refused), targets present in that Run, and a live tree equal to
398	the Run's snapshot (`REPAIR.SOURCE_MOVED`). It emits `RepairPlanV1`
399	(`repairplan2:` = `H('workflow.repair-plan', descriptor)`) bound to `snapshot2`,
400	`run2`, `plan2`, exact per-file edits (`replace|delete|create`, preimage digest from
401	the snapshot inventory, postimage digest and bytes; ≤ 4096 files, ≤ 16 MiB each,
402	≤ 64 MiB total), evidence requirements, the recipe's permitted edit scope (an edit
403	outside it is `REPAIR.EDIT_OUTSIDE_PERMITTED_SCOPE`), `applicable`, unmet
404	preconditions and limitations. Destructive unused-code recipes additionally require
405	native closed-world resolution evidence; an advisory similarity or runtime-cold
406	signal alone never authorizes deletion. Preview never writes.
407	
408	**The closed-world gate reads the evidence Run; the descriptor carries a
409	projection.** The guard covers **every `delete` and every `replace` edit** in the
410	plan — the unsafe-action set is those two actions, without qualification, and this
411	paragraph narrows it in no way. If the plan contains one, the prerequisite is
412	decided against the evidence Run's own native `ClosedWorldV2` (native §4.5) —
413	the record that contract closes at seven members — **before** any descriptor is
414	built: `deadCodeRepairEligible=false` reports
415	`REPAIR.CLOSED_WORLD_NOT_ESTABLISHED` with that record's own `reasons` in the
416	remedy, and an `imported-prepared-declared` evidence origin reports the same code,
417	because a DECLARED prepared expansion is not authority for an unsafe repair.
418	
419	`dynamicDispatch` is **not** a global veto and must not be read as one. Native
420	§4.5 makes dynamic-edge effects **target-relative**: `affected_targets` marks the
421	subjects a dynamic edge could reach, and §4.6 turns that into
422	`resolution-incomplete` for a universal negative **about an affected subject**.
423	So a present dynamic edge disqualifies the claims that depend on the subjects it
424	reaches; it does not by itself disqualify an unrelated target in the same Run.
425	The roles here are distinct and are not merged: preview **admits** each evidence
426	requirement's `relation`/`minResolution` against the registered vocabulary and its
427	relation's own ladder (`admit_atom`, which is vocabulary admission, not an
428	evidence judgement), and then **consumes** that requirement's own `satisfied`
429	value; the semantic sufficiency behind it is owned by native §4.6
430	`sufficiency_v2` and the §4.5 affected-target evidence, per requirement, and is
431	never collapsed into one flag.
432	
433	`RepairPlanDescriptor.closedWorld` is then the **five-field projection** of the
434	evidence record — `deadCodeRepairEligible`, `exportsClosed`,
435	`entryPointsRecognized`, `nonliteralLoading`, `externalConsumers`, with
436	`dynamicDispatch` and `reasons` dropped — and `repair.schema.json` closes it at
437	exactly those five, so a literal copy of `ClosedWorldV2` is refused there. **The
438	projection grants no evidence authority of its own.** It is a descriptor: no edit
439	to it can make a plan applicable, since the whole descriptor is the preimage of
440	`repairPlanId` (`H('workflow.repair-plan', descriptor)`) and apply requires a
441	security authorization bound to that exact `repairPlanId`, base snapshot and
442	project. The authority stays the sealed Run named by `evidenceRunId`: the
443	prerequisite above is decided against **that** Run's own full record, including
444	the two members the descriptor does not carry. No claim is made here that a later
445	step re-reads it — `repair verify` seals a **new** Run over the freshly
446	re-snapshotted tree (`appliedSnapshotId` → `verifiedSnapshotId`) and compares
447	remaining and net-new findings; it does not re-open the original evidence Run.
448	
449	**Apply** (`repair-apply`, mutation) is bound to the exact `repairPlanId`, base
450	snapshot and project by a security-unit authorization (`REPAIR.CONSENT_NOT_BOUND`);
451	CI requires policy consent. Current recipe trust and live authorization are checked
452	again immediately before apply. It journals `RepairApplyJournalV1` through
453	`PREPARING → STAGED → APPLYING → APPLIED → COMMITTED`: every postimage is written to a
454	same-directory temp and digest-verified, every preimage is re-verified against the
455	live file (`REPAIR.TARGET_PREIMAGE_MISMATCH` leaves `FAILED_CLEAN`), renames proceed in
456	ascending path order, then the tree is re-snapshotted (`appliedSnapshotId`) and the
457	receipt written. A fault during `APPLYING` restores every renamed target
458	(`FAILED_ROLLED_BACK`, rollback `completed`); a renamed target that is neither
459	preimage nor postimage is `RECOVERY_BLOCKED` with the paths listed and no automatic
460	action. Replaying apply with the same idempotency key returns the completed receipt
461	with a new replay delivery receipt and `replayed=true`; the original is preserved.
462	
463	**Recover** (`repair-recover`) is a closed table over journal state: PREPARING/STAGED
464	→ discard temps (`FAILED_CLEAN`); APPLYING → roll back renamed (`FAILED_ROLLED_BACK`)
465	or block if a target is unrecognized; APPLIED/INDETERMINATE → verify every exact
466	postimage and the complete applied-path set before re-snapshot and commit;
467	COMMITTED/FAILED_* → none; RECOVERY_BLOCKED → refuse (`HOST.IO_FAILURE`,
468	`REPAIR.RECOVERY_BLOCKED`, exit 4). Every recovery mutation requires an authorization
469	bound to this repairPlanId and journal requestId; inspection alone is read-only.
470	Restore verifies all available retained preimage hashes before its first write.
471	Corrupt bytes yield LEDGER.CORRUPT / REPAIR.PREIMAGE_CORRUPT (4) with no target change.
472	Unavailable bytes return an exact restore intent and REPAIR.RECOVERY_REQUIRES_BROKER,
473	without claiming rollback completed. Recovery never re-applies an edit.
474	
475	**Verify** (`verify`) always admits a **fresh snapshot** after apply; it never reuses
476	the pre-apply Run. If the fresh snapshot differs from `appliedSnapshotId` the step is
477	`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` / `REPAIR.SOURCE_MOVED` and no Run is sealed; otherwise
478	it seals a new authoritative Run and reports `VerificationOutcome`
479	(applied/verified snapshot, targets remaining, net-new findings). A separate immutable VerificationLinkV1 binds receiptId, verificationRunId, both
480	snapshots and the verification request/step. The apply receipt is never rewritten
481	and remains retained if verification fails.
482	
483	---
484	
485	## 7. Explicitly authorized test execution (AR-08)
486	
487	Repository code execution is disabled by default. `opensip test run` (request class
488	`execution`) is admitted only when: the security unit admits a `RepoExecutionGrantV2`

=== prose sec 2.2:
### 2.2 `typescript-v2` (replaces `typescript-v1.resolvedInputs`)

Retained **in the universe**: `tsconfigGraphHash`, `programRootFiles`,
`executionCapableResolution` (constant `false`: no TypeScript-side repository
execution is selected).

**Relocated to the context** (§2.4), and therefore *not* fields of the closed
`TypeScriptUniverseV2ResolvedInputs`, which is `additionalProperties: false`:
`compilerOptions` — now `TypeScriptConfigProjectionV2.honoredOptions` and
`strippedOptions`; `packageLockIdentity` — now
`TypeScriptNativeContextV2.lockfileIdentity`, with `lockfileKind` retained in the
universe as its kind projection; and `resolvedNodeModulesLayout` — now the
retained `ResolvedNodeModulesLayoutV1` record that
`TypeScriptNativeContextV2.nodeModulesLayoutDigest` names. An implementer building
a universe record from the older "Retained:" list produced a record that fails
admission; these three moved, they were not dropped.

`tsconfigGraphHash` is the **raw SHA-256 of `C(TypeScriptConfigGraphV1)`** — a
retained canonical record, not an H identity and not an opaque id. That record is
`{schemaVersion: 1, entryConfigPath, nodes}`, where `nodes` is the strictly ascending
unique-by-`path` array of every config file actually read, each
`{path, contentSha256, kind, extendsResolved}`: `contentSha256` is that file's
inventoried snapshot digest and `extendsResolved` is the ordered array of
project-relative paths its `extends` entries resolved to. Later entries take
precedence; repetitions are retained, and an empty array means no base config.
`entryConfigPath` selects the root config, or is null for synthesized configuration.
The record is a **required** binding input, and the binding
checks that `nodes[].path` is exactly the context's
`configProjection.configGraphPaths` set, that every node's digest is the snapshot's,
and that every edge names another node. Every node must be reachable from the
selected entry and the graph must be acyclic, so the universe key and the context
cannot describe two different config graphs.

`configOrigin` is **derived from that retained record, never asserted**:
`synthesized` exactly when the entry is null and `nodes` is empty; otherwise it
comes from the selected entry's kind (`jsconfig` for a jsconfig entry, otherwise
`tsconfig`). Node kind agrees with its path as specified by the schema and native
admission. A jsconfig entry extending a shared base remains a jsconfig program.
The universe's `configOrigin` must equal the derived value. This is the input
§2.4's agreement check needs; without the record the `tsconfig`/`jsconfig`
distinction was not derivable and two spellings minted two universe identities for
one admitted context.

Added: `schemaVersion=2`, `languageMode`, `configOrigin`,
`synthesizerVersion`, `synthesizedOptions`, `packageModuleType`, `allowJs`,
`checkJs`, `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `jsDiagnosticsEnabled`,
`resolutionCompletenessImplied=false`, `jsRootFiles`, `lockfileKind`,
`nodeModulesInReadSet` (`false` means bare specifiers are
`unresolved-module-specifier`, scope `external`; never an implicit install) and
`nativeContextId` — the identity of the **`TypeScriptNativeContextV2`** record of §2.4,
under the domain `native.context.typescript.v2`. It is never a `NativeContextV2`
(that record is the Rust context, §2.3), and a `typescript-v2` universe that names a
Rust-minted context refuses before PlanId (§2.4).

**`ResolvedNodeModulesLayoutV1`** is the record that digest names, and it is what
makes the ordinary TypeScript project — the one with dependencies — representable.
It is `{schemaVersion: 1, entries}`, where `entries` is strictly ascending and
unique by `installPath`, one row per installed package directory the resolver may
read: `{packageName, packageVersion, installPath, realPath, contentSha256}`.
`installPath` is the project-relative directory as the resolver walks it,
`realPath` is that directory after symlink or workspace-link resolution (equal to
`installPath` when there is no link, and otherwise itself an `installPath` of this
layout), and `contentSha256` is the raw SHA-256 of that package's manifest file
bytes, retained in the closure.

These rows are **not** snapshot inventory rows and must not be: the one shared
discovery rule prunes `node_modules` by path segment, so the layout is a retained
resolution observation of bytes the analysis read, joined by digest rather than by
snapshot membership. `nodeModulesInReadSet` is exactly
`nodeModulesLayoutDigest is not null`, the layout is a **required** binding input
whenever it is non-null, and a retained layout that no context selected is refused
rather than drifting into the resolution. With the layout present, bare specifiers
resolve normally; with it absent, `nodeModulesInReadSet=false` and every bare
specifier is an `unresolved-module-specifier` edge with scope `external` — never an
implicit install. Both branches are now constructible; before this record existed
only the second one was.

`SynthesizedCompilerOptionsV1` (deterministic function of the unit listing and
`package.json`; version 1 pinned): `allowJs=true`, `checkJs=false`,
`module=node16`, `moduleResolution=node16`, `target=es2022`, `jsx=preserve` iff any
`.jsx/.tsx` root exists else absent, `strict=false`, `skipLibCheck=true`,
`types=[]`, `noEmit=true`, roots = every `.ts/.tsx/.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx` file under
the unit excluding `node_modules`, `.git` and host ignore conventions. No option is
read from the environment. A synthesizer change is a universe change.

62	## 1. Invocation, step, attempt, Run (AR-08)
63	
64	An invocation is one host request. Its operational identity is `RequestId`, minted
65	before admission and retained for refusal as well as success. The invocation is an
66	ordered acyclic list of at most **64 steps**; `StepId` is the zero-based position.
67	Each admitted attempt of a step receives a fresh `ExecutionId`; a step has at most
68	**3 attempts**. Only `analysis` and `verify` steps seal or link a content-derived
69	`run2`. `comparison`, `query`, `render`, `import`, `repair-preview`, `repair-apply`,
70	`test-execution`, `native-preparation`, `mutation`, `export-delivery` and `doctor` are operational steps
71	that never mint a Run. Schema: `invocation-record.schema.json`.
72	
73	**Step DAG versus derivation DAG.** The step list is the operational workflow. Each
74	analysis/verify *attempt* owns exactly one derivation DAG (`exec-plan2`, at most
75	**1024 stages**) recorded in the attempt's `derivation` binding
76	(`planId`, `executionPlanId`, `stageCount`, `stagesCompleted`, `firstFailedStage`).
77	A step never depends on a stage and a stage never references a step. A retry on
78	identical admitted inputs may bind the same `exec-plan2` and the same Run; attempts
79	remain separately auditable.
80	
81	**Dependencies.** `dependsOn` names lower StepIds only (a forward or self reference is
82	`WORKFLOW.DEPENDENCY_CYCLE`, request-rejected). `requirement` is `required` or
83	`optional`; a required step may not depend on an optional step
84	(`WORKFLOW.REQUIRED_DEPENDS_ON_OPTIONAL`). `dependencyGate` is `completed` (every
85	dependency completed) or `terminal` (every dependency reached any terminal outcome;
86	lawful only for `render`/`export-delivery`, which project whatever happened). A
87	step whose gate is unmet is `skipped` with a typed `skipReason`. Step outcomes are
88	closed: `completed`, `rejected`, `failed`, `skipped`, `cancelled`, `abandoned`
89	(crash recovery only).
90	
91	**Retries.** `retryPolicy=idempotent-retry` is lawful only for `analysis`, `verify`,
92	`query`, `render`, `doctor` and `export-delivery`, only for `faultCause=ledger-busy`,
93	and within the 3-attempt budget; exhausting it is `LEDGER.BUSY_TIMEOUT` (4) with
94	detail `WORKFLOW.RETRY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`. `host-io` and every other fault are never
95	retried. `mutation`, `import`, `repair-preview`, `repair-apply`, `comparison`, `native-preparation` and `test-execution`
96	carry `retryPolicy=none` by schema; a spec violating this is refused.
97	
98	**Mutation idempotence and recovery.** Generic `mutation` steps use the bare
99	64-hex `H("workflow.mutation-intent", MutationReplayScopeV1)`. The closed retained
100	scope is exactly `{schemaVersion:1,requestId,stepId,projectId,operation}`, with
101	`operation` equal to `MutationParams.mutationClass`. This explicitly succeeds the
102	former undefined `{operation,projectId,effect preimage}` description. The key is
103	operational and scoped to one host-minted request and admitted immutable step;
104	different fresh requests never deduplicate each other's generic mutations.
105	`sourceStep` resolves inside that same retained invocation, whose admitted
106	parameters and completed dependency results are immutable. Before lookup or
107	replay the host validates the scope and full params, recomputes the key and
108	requires the retained invocation/project/step/operation binding; a caller cannot
109	nominate another invocation's scope or change effect inputs under an old key.
110	Receipt lookup is never an effect-authorization mechanism. A same-scope COMPLETED
111	receipt permits delivery replay with no second effect. Failure, unknown state or
112	incomplete execution requires the operation's existing recovery law, not blind
113	re-execution. Recovery started in a new request retains its own operational scope
114	and the explicit original journal/intent links required by §§6/12.
115	
116	Repair apply is the explicit content-derived exception: it is a dedicated
117	`repair-apply` step, excluded from generic MutationParams. It uses the raw SHA-256 of
118	canonical `{operation:"repair-apply",projectId,repairPlanId,baseSnapshotId}` as its
119	idempotency key. An equal completed key performs no second effect. The original
120	receipt is immutable; a replay delivery produces a separately identified receipt
121	with the new request/attempt binding and `replayed=true`. Mutation receipts use
122	`receipt2:` plus `H('workflow.mutation-receipt', receiptWithoutReceiptId)` and remain
123	retained when an effect or later verification fails. Read-only recovery inspection
124	is distinct from separately authorized recovery writes (§6).
125	
126	**Audit gate ownership.** An analysis step declares `verdictGate=self|delegated`.
127	`self` applies its Run verdict. `delegated` requires authoritative analysis and a
128	consuming comparison step: a completed failing Run then contributes operational
129	success with its RunId, while the comparison owns the regression gate. This lets
130	inherited findings remain visible without failing the PR. Missing required Coverage
131	still contributes indeterminate; delegation cannot hide an incomplete analysis.
132	The comparison result is a distinct closed `ComparisonStepResult`, never a Run.
133	
134	**Cancellation.** A signal is recorded with the phase at which it arrived.
135	*before-settle* (some required step not yet terminal): remaining steps are
136	`cancelled`, the aggregate is `interrupted` (130), and a Run committed by an earlier
137	step is named in the termination's `runId`. *after-settle* (every required step
138	already terminal): the aggregate is **not reclassified**; the settled class stands.
139	Per kind: an analysis attempt aborts and leaves no Run; an import discards its
140	staged bytes; a repair-apply honours cancellation only before `APPLYING`, and during
141	the bounded rename loop the journal, not the signal, decides (§6).
142	
143	**Aggregate termination (D9 ordering preserved).** Over required steps only:
144	`operational-failed` > `request-rejected` > `policy-failed` > `indeterminate` >
145	`success`. An optional step's rejection or failure never changes the aggregate.
146	Policy fail dominates indeterminate across steps exactly as inside one Run, and a
147	required operational fault dominates a committed failing Run (its `runId` is still
148	carried). Exit code derives from class by the fixed table only. Ties retain the first
149	termination carrying domain detail in step order, or the first termination when
150	none carries detail, so a useful comparison remedy is preserved.
151	
152	**Ephemeral analysis.** `--ephemeral` produces the second member of the closed
153	`AnalysisResult` union: `authority=ephemeral`, `durability=not-required`, no `runId`,
154	no receipt, only semantic `planId`/`evidenceId` so the result can be cited. It cannot
155	satisfy baseline adoption, repair preview/apply, verify or authoritative replay
156	(`WORKFLOW.EPHEMERAL_CANNOT_SUPPLY_AUTHORITY`, `REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE`, exit 2). A
157	failing ephemeral verdict terminates `policy-failed` with `authority=ephemeral`
158	instead of a `runId`; the branch contract admits exactly one of the two.
159	
160	**Default invocation.** `opensip` with no arguments is discovery then one durable
161	authoritative analysis (steps `analysis`, `render`). Retention is DEFAULTED
162	durable-unbounded (CD-RT-5), disclosed with the storage root before first write.
163	No policy file is written implicitly.
164	
165	---
166	
167	## 2. Portable baseline and runnable prior detector (AR-10)

1121	and retains that resolved set and its authority provenance; the evaluator does
1122	not consult today's wall clock. Replay evaluates the historical sealed set;
1123	new analysis and repair authorization resolve current expiry and revocation
1124	again. A historical waiver result is never a fresh grant.
1125	
1126	The complete closure includes bytes for each policy, waiver, rule program,
1127	configuration, analysis specification, scope descriptor, semantic grant, owner
1128	source set, source inventory, VCS observation, stage spec, native context frame,
1129	native universe frame, capability manifest, registered schema, import
1130	payload/mapping/correspondence/build/observation, fact payload, Coverage payload,
1131	finding parameters, program predicate and predicate witness referenced anywhere in
1132	this graph — that is, the preimage of every digest whose retention mode is
1133	`preimage`, with the three named exceptions recomputed or owner-retained as §3
1134	states. For a native context or universe this reaches the nested semantic records
1135	it names and their raw members: the dependency source set, its packages' file
1136	manifests and every manifest member's bytes at exactly its declared length; the
1137	unified features; the cargo config projection and the projected config file bytes;
1138	and every inert prepared-output row's bytes. A replayable Run retains them all.
1139	The host recomputes all blob hashes and all semantic identities, validates each
1140	payload with the exact admitted schema and its semantic admission rules, and
1141	rejects missing, extra authoritative roots, wrong-kind, cross-Plan/cross-source
1142	or unresolved references. Unreferenced CAS blobs are not evaluation inputs.
1143	Snapshot config/scope, Plan config/scope and native-context source correspondence
1144	must agree. **The Plan's deterministic `budget` must equal, exactly and by type,
1145	the `analysis.budget` of the committed resolved semantic configuration the same
1146	Plan names.** The value is committed in two places and neither silently wins: a
1147	legitimate budget override enters the **resolved semantic configuration first**
1148	(admission-and-qualification §1.1's layered resolution), and the Plan then
1149	carries that same `{unit, limit}`. A Plan whose inline budget contradicts its own
1150	configuration is refused before any evaluation. Both values already enter PlanId,
1151	so this changes no identity, replay or determinism property; what it fixes is
1152	that two conforming implementations would otherwise disagree on *admission*.
1153	Every view's facts/scopes/Coverage agree on Plan source, universes,
1154	relation/rung and producer; every source anchor must name an inventoried blob,
1155	and the number of anchors must be the one the relation registry's `anchorLaw`
1156	states for that relation. Coverage scopes partition the claimed universe without
1157	overlaps or omissions, and a `complete` result for a rung the registry marks
1158	total over the inventory (`file@enumerated`) must carry a fact for every
1159	inventoried subject it claims to have examined — a fact that agrees with **that
1160	scope** on its own snapshot, relation, rung and *both* universes. The fact/scope
1161	join above is existential, so in a view carrying two universes a fact of one
1162	lawfully sits beside a scope of the other and must not discharge its obligation.
1163	No arbitrary payload schema supplied by an import becomes an admitted schema.
1164	
1165	## 4. Evaluation and proof verification
1166	
1167	The deterministic evaluator consumes only the Plan-bound, schema-admitted
1168	finite fact views, Coverage, imported evidence, declarative program, policy and
1169	waivers. The declarative rule program defines the exact subject enumeration,
1170	relation/rung, typed field filter, quantifier, deterministic work bound and
1171	emission condition for each predicate. Query planning is an optimization only:
1172	a retained full-scan reference must agree on selected facts. Neither a provider
1173	nor a witness supplies its own expected result or filter. All consumed data are
1174	listed in the proof's evaluationInputRefs; no hidden lookup is allowed.
1175	
1176	A predicate proof binds rule, subject, predicate, operation, admitted inputs,
1177	scopes, value and a retained witness digest. The closed witness record contains
1178	schemaVersion=2, program predicate digest, sorted matching fact IDs, sorted
1179	Coverage IDs, optional integer count limit and sorted child-predicate IDs.
1180	The program predicate digest is the §3 `program-predicate` record, which addresses
1181	the exact node of the admitted rule program this proof discharges; the predicate
1182	ID and the child predicate IDs are that section's node addresses, not free
1183	labels. An atomic witness names no children; boolean witnesses name only earlier
1184	nodes in the same subject/rule DAG, and each named child must itself be proven
1185	for the same rule and subject. Predicate IDs are unique and the DAG is bounded
1186	by the rule program's admitted work bound. Witness facts must be exactly those
1187	selected by the program over the complete admitted view, not merely a subset
1188	chosen by the producer. Counts count distinct selected fact IDs. The verifier
1189	recomputes scope membership, matches, completeness and each result, and then
1190	recomputes finding fingerprints, findings, rule outcomes and aggregate verdict.
1191	Missing witness bytes is retention loss, not a false predicate.
1192	
1193	| Predicate | Positive/complete case | Incomplete case |
1194	|---|---|---|
1195	| exists | true on a matching fact; false only on complete absence | true on a known match, otherwise indeterminate |
1196	| none | false on a known match; true only on complete absence | false on a known match, otherwise indeterminate |
1197	| count-at-most N | false once more than N distinct matches exist; true when complete count ≤ N | false above N, otherwise indeterminate |
1198	| all-covered | true only with admitted resolution-complete coverage for the requested universe/rung | indeterminate |
1199	| and / or / not | strong Kleene three-valued logic; false dominates and, true dominates or | unresolved value propagates unless dominated |

318	cardinality, so every published predicate over the array — the `file` row's

### 1.4 Mixed repositories and workspace units (R1)

The v1 rule ("deepest root, then `Cargo.toml` > `tsconfig.json`") was wrong: in a
repository whose root holds both `Cargo.toml` and `package.json`/`tsconfig.json`
every TypeScript file fell into the Rust unit and silently left the TypeScript
program. Units are now **per language family and program membership**, and may
share a root.

**Reference discovery model** (`discover_units`, `assign_membership` in the model;
records `WorkspaceUnitV2`, `FileMembershipRowV1`, `UnitMembershipV1`). The root
discovery boundary and trust decision remain the security/foundation owners'
(DR-103); this contract defines what happens inside that boundary.

`WorkspaceUnitV2` (closed): `{unitOrdinal, rootPath, languageFamily: rust|tsjs|none,
languageMode, unitKind: cargo-workspace|cargo-package|ts-program|js-program|syntax-only,
markerPath, markerSha256, recognizerId, recognizerVersion, provenance:
EXPLICIT|DISCOVERED|DEFAULTED, memberPackageRoots[]}`.

- **U-1 (one unit per directory and language family)** A directory holding
  `Cargo.toml` yields a `rust` unit; a directory holding `tsconfig.json`,
  `jsconfig.json` or `package.json` yields exactly one `tsjs` unit whose mode is
  chosen by precedence `tsconfig.json` (→ `ts-tsconfig`/`js-allowjs`) >
  `jsconfig.json` (→ `js-allowjs`) > `package.json` (→ `js-synthesized`). The
  precedence selects the mode **within** `tsjs`; it never removes the co-located
  `rust` unit. A root with both markers has two units with the same `rootPath`
  (`units-colocated-cargo-and-package-json-root-keeps-both-languages`).
- **U-2 (Cargo workspace folding)** A `Cargo.toml` package inside a Cargo
  workspace root's tree is folded into the workspace unit as a member package
  (Cargo resolves the workspace as one program); it is listed in
  `memberPackageRoots`, not as a separate unit. A standalone package outside any
  workspace is its own `cargo-package` unit. **Explicit roots are unit
  selection, never loss of Cargo workspace semantics (post-reset v2 A-3/P22):**
  naming a Cargo workspace root explicitly yields exactly the automatic result
  for that unit (members folded, member `target` output pruned, a member's
  `src/target` still source); naming a member package alone selects that package
  as its own `cargo-package` unit, and files of the unselected root or siblings
  are honest `no-program-unit-for-language` rows, neither claimed nor
  over-ignored (`units-explicit-cargo-workspace-root-keeps-member-folding-and-member-target-pruning`).
- **U-3 (deterministic membership within a language)** A file's family is fixed
  by extension (`.rs` → `rust`; `.ts/.tsx/.mts/.cts/.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx` → `tsjs`).
  It belongs to the **deepest unit of its own family** whose root prefixes its
  path. Units of another family never claim it. Nested monorepo packages
  (`packages/web/tsconfig.json` under a root `tsconfig.json`) are therefore
  distinct `tsjs` units and the deeper one wins for its subtree
  (`units-nested-monorepo-deepest-within-language-and-workspace-folding`).
- **U-4 (no source erasure; honest unsupported files)** Every snapshot inventory
  file appears in exactly one `FileMembershipRowV1`: `program-member`;
  `syntax-only` with reason `no-program-unit-for-language` (a `.rs` file with no
  enclosing Rust unit: semantic rungs `unknown`, cause `no-program-unit`),
  `grammar-only` (bundled grammar, no program) or `host-ignore-convention`
  (the file lies inside a pruned tree of the shared rule below); or
  `unsupported-file` with reason `no-bundled-grammar`, listed in
  `unsupportedFiles`. `erasedFiles` is a schema-constant empty array
  (`maxItems 0`) and the model refuses a membership that does not cover the
  inventory exactly once.
- **U-4a (one shared discovery rule; post-reset MUST-3)** The host ignore
  conventions and unit enumeration are stated once, in
  `docs/coop/design-corrections/discovery-defaults.py`, and consumed by both
  `discover_units`/`assign_membership`/`unit_scope_descriptor`/`typescript_mode`
  here and by the security discovery instrument (security S3). Pruned trees,
  by **exact path segment** (never substring): dependency trees (`node_modules`),
  VCS trees (`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.jj`) and Cargo build output (a `target`
  segment whose parent directory holds `Cargo.toml`, an actual Cargo root known
  from the units: workspace root or folded member package). `packages/target/index.ts`
  and `src/target/x.ts` are ordinary program members; `target/debug/x.rs` under
  a root `Cargo.toml` is `host-ignore-convention`. A marker inside a pruned tree
  (every `node_modules/<pkg>/package.json`, a `Cargo.toml` under `node_modules`)
  is never a unit and never a Cargo root; each pruned tree is reported once in
  `UnitDiscoveryV1.prunedTrees` (`PrunedTreeV1 {path, reason, markerCount}`) and
  its anchor enters `excludedPathPrefixes`. Pruning is a discovery rule, not a
  read-set exemption: bytes a program later reads from a pruned tree
  (`node_modules` in the TypeScript read set, §2.2/§9.4) enter the snapshot read

"""Refresh the four unit source-pins files IN A DISPOSABLE COPY ONLY.
Usage: python -I -B repin.py <disposable-root>   (never run against `work`)"""
import hashlib, json, pathlib, sys
ROOT = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
assert 'disposable' in str(ROOT), 'refuse: repin only ever runs in a disposable copy'
DC = ROOT / 'docs/coop/design-corrections'
changed = []
for pin, key in [('foundation/source-pins.v1.json', 'files'), ('workflows/source-pins.v1.json', 'files'),
                 ('native/source-pins.v2.json', 'pins'), ('security/source-pins.v1.json', 'pins')]:
    p = DC / pin
    d = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
    rows = d[key]
    items = rows.items() if isinstance(rows, dict) else [(r['path'], r) for r in rows]
    for path, row in items:
        cur = hashlib.sha256((ROOT / path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        if isinstance(row, dict) and 'sha256' in row and row['sha256'] != cur:
            row['sha256'] = cur; changed.append((pin, path))
        elif isinstance(row, str) and row != cur:
            rows[path] = cur; changed.append((pin, path))
    p.write_text(json.dumps(d, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n', encoding='utf-8')
print(json.dumps({'repinnedIn': str(ROOT), 'rows': len(changed)}, indent=1))

overlaps or omissions, and a `complete` result for a rung the registry marks
total over the inventory (`file@enumerated`) must carry a fact for every
inventoried subject it claims to have examined — a fact that agrees with **that
scope** on its own snapshot, relation, rung and *both* universes. The fact/scope
join above is existential, so in a view carrying two universes a fact of one
lawfully sits beside a scope of the other and must not discharge its obligation.
"""
NEW = """states for that relation.

**Coverage scopes partition, and the two halves of that word have different
owners.** *Disjointness* is the general rule and applies to every relation: two
Coverage scopes of one view that share the **full owning tuple** — the same
`(snapshotId, relation, resolution, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse)` — carry
disjoint subject sets, so no subject is claimed twice under one interpretation.
This is decidable from the retained scopes alone and is a producer obligation
stated here; a differing tuple is a different claim, not an overlap, which is why
the same path may lawfully appear under two universes.

*Omission* is **not** a general rule and is never inferred. A scope owes a
complete enumeration only where the relation registry gives its rung a
`coverageTotality` row, which today is `file@enumerated` alone: a snapshot
inventories exactly the files it contains, so a `complete` result there must carry
a fact for every inventoried subject it claims to have examined — a fact that
agrees with **that scope** on its own snapshot, relation, rung and *both*
universes. `package@manifest-declared` and `vcs-change@vcs-reported` have no row
and owe nothing, because most paths declare no package and most were not changed.

boundary rather than an omission**: native §1.2 records that the enumerator's
attribution of symbols to files is trusted and **not re-derivable from the
retained Run**, no enumeration of the symbol universe is published, and inventing
one would be fabricated evidence. Reading "without omissions" as a universal
obligation would therefore make the clause either unenforceable or a demand for
evidence the design deliberately does not claim.

This does **not** make `complete` vacuous where no totality row exists. It remains
a claim about the **examined** partition, and it is held to that claim by the
entry's own committed evidence: RC-0 decides the relation's registered
`(relation, rung)` pair before any fact is read, RC-1 keeps enumeration
completeness separate from resolution completeness, RC-2 forces
`unresolvedEdgeClasses` to equal the admitted `unresolved-edge` facts of the view
and never lets a zero edge count imply `complete`, `examinedUniverse` carries the
counts, and `partial`/`not-attempted`/`unknown` with a disclosed deficiency stay
representable so nothing is forced into a false `complete`. The fact/scope join
above is existential, so in a view carrying two universes a fact of one lawfully
sits beside a scope of the other and must not discharge its obligation.

`run2`, `plan2`, exact per-file edits (`replace|delete|create`, preimage digest from
the snapshot inventory, postimage digest and bytes; ≤ 4096 files, ≤ 16 MiB each,
≤ 64 MiB total), evidence requirements, the recipe's permitted edit scope (an edit
outside it is `REPAIR.EDIT_OUTSIDE_PERMITTED_SCOPE`), `applicable`, unmet
preconditions and limitations. Destructive unused-code recipes additionally require
native closed-world resolution evidence; an advisory similarity or runtime-cold
signal alone never authorizes deletion. Preview never writes.

**The closed-world gate reads the evidence Run; the descriptor carries a
projection.** The guard covers **every `delete` and every `replace` edit** in the
plan — the unsafe-action set is those two actions, without qualification, and this
paragraph narrows it in no way. If the plan contains one, the prerequisite is
decided against the evidence Run's own native `ClosedWorldV2` (native §4.5) —
